finding: Partial, rational trivial norm-one isotype only: for fixed positive symmetric width and test supported over norm > 1+ε, the printed passage claims the full interior-zero multiplicity trace at s=0 and the displayed max{N(ρ),[(s−1)/2]} at shifted boundary zeros for s>0. On the actual separated half-twisted radial quotient of Theorems.RationalRadialHilbertQuotient, a continuous linear functional giving the m-th Mellin moment on compactly supported original profiles with exponent z at |Re z|=α requires 2m+1<s. Pullback through the quotient map, the actual weighted-norm transport to L²(dx), and Hahn–Banach give the necessary log-jet estimate of Props.BoundaryLogJet. The nondecaying tail diverges at equality; at s=1 even the order-zero evaluation is excluded at a boundary point, while both the introductory max and the later min cap in (10.2.2.5) would keep that order for a boundary zero. For the printed half twist use z=ρ−1/2; no boundary zero is asserted to exist for fixed positive width and half twist. No sufficient descent, totality, trace class, or degree-zero trace is proved. The proof of Theorem 9.3.2.6 reverses the nesting of the displayed kernels; the cited Theorem 10.3.2.1 assumes s>1. RationalRadialStripTrace concerns a scalar identity, not the operator trace.
retry: Reduce each finite-unit averaged two-mode rational LF stage to a real Schwartz unramified input preserving theta and both zero modes, by finite valuation strata and diagonal reindexing as in rational-radial-boundary-jet.md, or prove continued Mellin factorization directly on every actual radial LF generator. Use the resulting jet vanishing to descend all admissible jets (strict boundary threshold), then prove that their common kernel equals the closed theta range, including at s=0. For the actual supported convolution on that quotient, prove summable trace-class control and that the trace is exhausted by those zero blocks, with a separate degree-zero proof rather than the s>1 citation. General fields and nontrivial isotypes also need their actual norm, theta, and operator identifications.
